papers.title: Effects of RhBNP combined with immune modulation on immune function and short-term clinical outcomes in patients with atrial fibrillation and heart failure.
papers.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
papers.authors: Li S, Li G, Xie R, Jin G
papers.abstract:
Heart failure (HF) and atrial fibrillation (AF) commonly coexist, sharing underlying pathophysiology and risk factors, which leads to high morbidity and complex clinical management. While recombinant human B-type natriuretic peptide (rhBNP) is used for acute HF, its combined effect with traditional Chinese medicine for immune regulation in HF patients with persistent AF remains unclear.
This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and immunological impact of rhBNP combined with an immunomodulatory therapy in patients with HF and permanent AF.
In this randomized, prospective, controlled trial, 40 hospitalized patients with HF (NYHA class II-III, LVEF ≤40%) and permanent AF were enrolled. Participants were randomly assigned to receive conventional therapy alone (Control group, n = 20) or conventional therapy plus intravenous rhBNP and oral Zhenqi Fuzheng Granules for 7 days (Treatment group, n = 20).
Compared to the control group, the treatment group showed significantly greater reductions in BNP levels and greater improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Immunophenotyping analysis revealed that the treatment group had significantly increased absolute counts of CD3+ and CD4+ T lymphocytes and a higher CD4+/CD8+ ratio.
Adjunctive therapy combining rhBNP and immunomodulation in HF-AF patients significantly improves cardiac function, and is associated with improved short-term clinical outcomes. This suggests a promising multi-mechanistic therapeutic approach for this patient population.

papers.title: Two Older Adult Patients With Anorexia and Cachexia Following Refractory Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare Complex Pulmonary Disease Given Acupuncture Treatment to Improve Appetite and Food Intake.
papers.journal: The American journal of case reports
papers.authors: Maekura T, Miki K, Kida H, Maekura R
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Refractory Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare complex pulmonary disease (MAC-PD) is often complicated by anorexia, weight loss, and cachexia. This report describes 2 older adult patients with anorexia and cachexia following refractory MAC-PD given acupuncture treatment to improve appetite and food intake. CASE REPORT Case 1 was a man in his 70s with cavitary nodular bronchiectatic MAC-PD diagnosed 7 years earlier based on the 2007 American Thoracic Society/Infectious Diseases Society of America (ATS/IDSA) criteria. His chest radiographic lesions had progressively worsened, with persistent smear positivity despite multidrug chemotherapy. He developed complete anorexia and eating-related dyspnea; his body weight decreased to 35.4 kg (body mass index [BMI] 11.8 kg/m²). Case 2 was a woman in her 60s who was diagnosed with nodular bronchiectatic MAC-PD with cavities, which developed into a giant cavity, 4 years earlier. She developed severe anorexia and postprandial dyspnea, and her body weight was 31.0 kg (BMI 13.2 kg/m²). Both patients received manual acupuncture at CV12, ST36, LU9, and individualized points 3 times weekly for 3 weeks. Appetite on a 100-mm visual analog scale, energy intake, body weight, and serum albumin improved in both patients. Sputum acid-fast bacillus (AFB) smear status and radiographic findings were unchanged. No adverse events occurred. CONCLUSIONS Nine acupuncture sessions over 3 weeks improved appetite, dietary intake, and nutritional indices in 2 cachectic patients with refractory MAC-PD without altering bacteriological or radiological disease activity. Acupuncture merits consideration as adjunctive care for anorexia in this setting. Controlled studies are needed.

papers.title: [Expert consensus on testosterone supplementation to alleviate aging-related symptoms in men (2026 edition)].
papers.authors: Male Health Branch of Chinese Health Management Association
papers.abstract: Aging is frequently accompanied by a variety of symptoms and changes in physiological indicators that impair men's quality of life. Alleviating aging-related symptoms and improving quality of life in men has become an important public-health goal. Testosterone levels gradually decline in men with advancing age. Accumulating evidence in recent years suggests that exogenous testosterone supplementation may ameliorate selected aging-related symptoms and enhance men's health status. This consensus was developed by the Male Health Management Branch of the Chinese Health Management Association, bringing together experts from endocrinology, andrology, traditional Chinese medicine, nutrition and other disciplines. Based on the latest evidence-based medical evidence, 21 recommendations were formulated focusing on key issues including ameliorating aging-related symptoms, appropriate candidates, risk assessment, medication strategies and monitoring protocols of testosterone supplementaion. It aims to provide guidance for clinicians on the scientific and standardized application of testosterone supplementation to alleviate aging-related symptoms in men.

papers.title: Acupuncture Mediates the Treatment of Childhood Pneumonia via Modulation of Lung ADRB2.
papers.journal: QJM : monthly journal of the Association of Physicians
papers.authors: Liu L, Qin W, Xu X, Zhong A, Cai W, Liang J et al.
papers.abstract:
Childhood pneumonia (CP) remains a major cause of pediatric hospitalization and mortality. Antibiotic resistance and drug-related adverse reactions highlight the need for safe adjunctive treatments. The β₂-adrenergic receptor (ADRB2) is associated with airway reactivity and inflammatory responses. Acupuncture has been reported to modulate autonomic and immune functions; however, its precise molecular mechanism in CP remains unclear.
Clinical outcomes were evaluated alongside transcriptomic analyses and animal experiments. The transcriptomic analyses comprised a pediatric PBMC dataset (GSE261482) and an independent mouse lung RNA-sequencing dataset (GSE325662). An LPS-induced juvenile mouse model was established to assess lung pathology, inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-10), and ADRB2 expression. Salbutamol and ICI-118551 were used to examine ADRB2-related effects.
Acupuncture showed significant adjunctive benefit, improving day-5 efficacy (P = 0.001), day-7 efficacy (P < 0.001), and day-5 clinical scores (P = 0.002), while shortening hospital stay (P < 0.001) without serious adverse reactions. Transcriptomic analysis implicated adrenergic signaling, particularly ADRB2, in CP. In juvenile mice, acupuncture reduced lung inflammation and modulated cytokine levels and ADRB2 expression. These findings suggest an association between ADRB2-related signalling and the pulmonary inflammatory response to acupuncture.
Acupuncture was associated with improved clinical outcomes in CP and attenuated lung inflammation in an LPS-induced juvenile mouse model. ADRB2-related adrenergic signaling may be involved in this anti-inflammatory effect. These results support the potential role of acupuncture as an adjunctive intervention for CP, although further studies are needed to confirm the causal contribution of ADRB2 and to define the underlying cell-specific mechanisms.

papers.title: Mechanisms underlying the effects of Buyang Huanwu Decoction against sepsis-induced ARDS using network pharmacology and experimental validation.
papers.authors: Tan W, Wang C, Liu X, Deng J, Sang Z, Hu X
papers.abstract:
Buyang Huanwu Decoction (BYHW), a classic formula from Yilin Gaicuo Qing Dynasty, is indicated for stroke in patients with qi deficiency and blood stasis in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia. In traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), the pathogenesis of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is associated with qi deficiency, blood stasis, and heat-toxin obstructing the lungs, which align with the therapeutic actions of this formula.
To investigate the effects of BYHW on sepsis-induced ARDS and the mechanisms underlying these effects.
ARDS was induced through LPS treatment in wild-type and eNOS-deficient (eNOS-/-) mice. The components of BYHW were analyzed using UPLC-UV-MS. Potential associated targets and pathways were predicted by network pharmacology and molecular docking experiments. Relevant protein and mRNA expression levels were assessed by Western blot analysis, immunofluorescence analysis, or qPCR.
BYHW significantly improving the hypothermia, elevated plasma levels of IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-6, the lung index and injury induced by LPS in wild-type (WT) mice. However, these effects of BYHW were markedly in eNOS-/- mice. LPS downregulated AQP1 protein expression and upregulated Cav-1 protein expression and the p-P65/P65 ratio in both groups but increased the p-IκB/IκB ratio only in the WT mice. Pretreatment of BYHW increased the expression of eNOS and AQP1, decreased the Cav-1 expression and P65/IκB phosphorylation in WT mice, but the action on the P65/IκB phosphorylation and AQP1 expression were abrogated in eNOS-/- mice.
BYHW protect against sepsis-induced ARDS may be related to decrease the eNOS-NF-κB-mediated synthesis of inflammatory cytokines and upregulation of AQP1 expression.

papers.title: Mechanisms of Traditional Chinese Medicine-Derived Active Components in the Treatment of Alzheimer's Disease: A Comprehensive Review.
papers.authors: Tian Y, Guo J, Lin X, Zhang F, Xie J, Hou X et al.
papers.abstract:
Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive cognitive decline and multifactorial pathology. Because AD involves interacting pathological processes, the limited efficacy of conventional single-target therapies has increased interest in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) and other natural medicines with multi-target pharmacological actions. TCM-derived active components originate from medicinal materials used in traditional practice and are evaluated using modern pharmacological approaches. Their source medicines have diverse traditional-use backgrounds. Some have historical associations with memory or cognitive symptoms, whereas many others were traditionally used for broader deficiency, phlegm, blood-stasis, heat, or related syndromic patterns. These records provide ethnopharmacological context for the source medicines but should not be taken as historical evidence for the anti-AD activity of their isolated constituents.
This review synthesizes current evidence on the mechanisms of TCM-derived bioactive components in AD while incorporating relevant traditional-use information on their source medicines. Particular attention is given to their multi-target actions and emerging mechanisms involving ferroptosis, mitophagy, and the gut-brain axis.
Mechanistic literature published between January 2019 and November 2025 was retrieved from Ovid MEDLINE, PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science. Ovid MEDLINE and PubMed were searched separately to maximize retrieval across indexed and additional PubMed records, with overlapping records removed during deduplication. Traditional-use information was evaluated separately for the source medicines. A targeted search of PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov was also conducted to assess human interventional evidence for compounds covered in the review, with trial-registration information updated through August 2026.
Current preclinical findings suggest that TCM active components may produce coordinated preclinical pharmacological effects through multiple pathways, including the inhibition of β-amyloid (Aβ) production and deposition, regulation of tau aggregation and phosphorylation, alleviation of neuroinflammation and oxidative stress, improvement of mitophagy and iron metabolism disorders, and modulation of gut microbiota homeostasis. Among these components, saponins show broad mechanistic coverage. Flavonoids, polysaccharides, and other bioactive substances have likewise shown anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, together with protective effects on synaptic function, in preclinical models. These mechanistic findings were derived predominantly from cellular and animal studies, with computational analyses providing mainly hypothesis-generating support. Human evidence was available for only a small subset of compounds and was not uniformly positive. Huperzine A has progressed to controlled clinical testing but has shown mixed efficacy findings; resveratrol demonstrated CNS exposure and biomarker activity without consistent cognitive benefit; curcumin did not show efficacy in a placebo-controlled AD trial; and favorable signals from ginseng studies were limited by open-label designs and the use of whole preparations rather than isolated ginsenosides.
The available evidence supports broad preclinical activity of TCM-derived components across several interconnected AD-related processes, but the strength of mechanistic support varies markedly among compounds and pathways. Human translation remains limited and inconsistent, and current clinical data do not establish disease-modifying efficacy for the compounds reviewed. Further development should therefore be guided by the main uncertainty surrounding each candidate-whether mechanistic causality, reproducibility, systemic or CNS exposure, preparation standardization, or clinical efficacy-rather than by a fixed sequence of technologies.

papers.title: Stepwise acupuncture exploration followed by ultrasound-guided needle-knife release combined with local infiltration for chronic intercostal muscle-related myofascial pain: A case report.
papers.authors: Ou Y, Li D, Li G, Li H
papers.abstract:
Intercostal muscle-related myofascial pain can be difficult to localize when superficial tenderness is absent because the muscles lie deep to the thoracic musculature and close to the pleura. We report a case in which stepwise muscle-specific acupuncture provided ancillary localization information before targeted treatment.
A 73-year-old man presented with a 3-year history of persistent right posterolateral chest wall heaviness and dull pain, predominantly involving the fourth to tenth intercostal spaces. The resting numerical rating scale (NRS) score was 8, and no definite superficial tender point was identified.
Clinical and imaging evaluations excluded more plausible cardiopulmonary, pleural, osseous, spinal, herpetic, or neuropathic causes. More than 1 month of sequential acupuncture targeting the trapezius, rhomboid, multifidus, erector spinae, and serratus muscles produced no meaningful improvement. When exploration reached the suspected deep intercostal layer, ultrasound-guided acupuncture reproduced the habitual pain and produced mild relief. This response was interpreted as hypothesis-generating localization information rather than confirmatory evidence and contributed to a provisional diagnosis of intercostal muscle-related myofascial pain.
The patient underwent 4 weekly sessions of ultrasound-guided needle-knife release combined with local infiltration of 0.25% lidocaine and compound betamethasone. The intercostal anatomy and needle tip were monitored in real time using an out-of-plane approach.
The NRS score decreased from 8 to 5 immediately after the first treatment and further decreased to 1 one week after the fourth treatment. Pain completely resolved at the 1-, 3-, and 6-month follow-ups, with no treatment-related adverse events.
Stepwise muscle-specific acupuncture may provide ancillary localization information when conventional examination cannot identify a deep chest wall pain generator. Ultrasound-guided needle-knife release combined with local infiltration targeting the suspected intercostal muscle was associated with sustained improvement and may represent a potential treatment approach for selected patients with deep intercostal muscle-related myofascial pain.

papers.title: Association between dampness syndrome severity and hyperuricemia after accounting for adiposity: A cross-sectional study.
papers.authors: Luo W, Liu W, Chen T, Xiang L, Liu M, Lu L et al.
papers.abstract: Dampness syndrome is a symptom-based traditional Chinese medicine pattern frequently observed in individuals with metabolic disorders. However, whether dampness syndrome severity provides information on hyperuricemia (HUA) beyond conventional adiposity indicators remains unclear. This study examined the association between dampness syndrome severity and HUA and evaluated whether this association persisted after accounting for adiposity. This cross-sectional study used retrospective health-examination data from adults in 2024. Dampness syndrome severity was assessed using the Dampness Syndrome Scale of Chinese Medicine (DSSCM). Multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline analyses were used to examine the association between DSSCM score and HUA. Body mass index (BMI) was included in the fully adjusted model, with waist circumference and waist-to-height ratio examined in sensitivity analyses. Because the DSSCM includes an explicit body obesity item, an additional sensitivity analysis recalculated the DSSCM score after excluding this item. Robust Poisson regression was performed to estimate prevalence ratios because HUA was common in the study population. Exploratory BMI-decomposition analysis was interpreted as statistical decomposition rather than causal mediation. Among 5973 participants, 3173 (53.1%) had HUA. In the model adjusted for demographic, renal, metabolic, and lifestyle covariates but not BMI, each 10-point increase in DSSCM score was weakly associated with higher odds of HUA (odds ratio = 1.041; 95% confidence interval: 1.004-1.079; P = .028). After additional adjustment for BMI, the association was attenuated and was no longer statistically significant (odds ratio = 1.011; 95% confidence interval: 0.975-1.048; P = .558). Sensitivity analyses using waist circumference and waist-to-height ratio as alternative adiposity indicators yielded consistent nonsignificant results. After excluding the body obesity item from the DSSCM score, the association was further weakened in multivariable models. BMI-stratified analyses showed no significant association across BMI strata. The association between dampness syndrome severity and HUA was substantially attenuated after accounting for adiposity. The DSSCM may help characterize symptom burden in integrative health assessment, but it was not independently associated with prevalent HUA after adjustment for adiposity indicators.

papers.title: True Versus Sham Thread Embedding Acupuncture for Spasticity-Related Symptoms and Disabilities in Multiple Sclerosis: Study Protocol of a Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.authors: Vaez-Tehrani M, Nahayati MA, Mosa-Farkhani E, Shafaei S, Nematshahi M, Bahrami-Taghanaki H
papers.abstract: Introduction: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune disease and one of the most common causes of non-traumatic disability in young adults, with over 2.8 million individuals worldwide. Spasticity affects nearly 80% of people with MS (PwMS), contributing to pain, gait disturbance, bowel/bladder dysfunction, sleep/mood disorders, and impaired quality of life. The complex condition known as Spasticity-Plus syndrome is gaining attention. Current pharmacological treatments are limited by side effects and short duration of benefits. Thread Embedding Acupuncture (TEA), which involves embedding absorbable polydioxanone (PDO) sutures into acupoints, offers prolonged stimulation and has shown promise in managing spasticity, particularly after stroke. Several randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have reported positive effects in MS. This is a study that protocol aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of True TEA (TTEA) compared with Sham TEA (STEA) in reducing spasticity and improving mobility and related symptoms among PwMS. Methods: This is a protocol of a randomized, sham-controlled, patient-, assessor- and analyst-blinded, superiority clinical trial. Thirty-eight eligible PwMS with moderate-to-severe spasticity will be randomized 1:1 to either TTEA or STEA. Both groups will undergo puncture at the same 30 acupoints but only the TTEA group will receive PDO thread implantation. The primary outcome is change in disability (EDSS). Secondary outcomes are Numeric Rating Scale for Spasticity (NRS-S), walking ability (MSWS-12), activities of daily living (Barthel Index), pain (McGill Pain Questionnaire), fatigue (MFIS), sleep quality (PSQI), urinary symptoms (ABSST), mood (HADS), quality of life (EQ-5D-5L), overall treatment satisfaction, willingness to repeat and recommendation to others. Assessments will be conducted at baseline, 4 weeks, and 12 weeks post-intervention. Intention-to-treat analysis will be performed. Perspective: To our knowledge this trial will be the first RCT to evaluate TEA in spasticity-related symptoms in PwMS. By using a sham-controlled design, it will determine whether TEA confers benefits beyond needle puncture alone. Findings may provide evidence for incorporating TEA as a complementary option in MS symptom management and inform future larger-scale trials. Trial registration: IRCT20121228011912N8 (22 March 2024; Updated: 13 July 2026).

papers.title: Exploring Perspectives of Parturient Women and the Obstetric Team: Towards an Integrative Obstetric Care Model.
papers.authors: Ben-Arye E, Gressel O, Yahalom M, Cohen VG, Zur N, Sher ML et al.
papers.abstract: Objectives: Integrative medicine programs are increasingly being implemented in clinical settings, including gynecology and obstetrics. This study explores an integrative obstetric and maternity care (IObM) model designed for real-life peri-labor settings, comparing perspectives among parturient women to obstetric healthcare professionals (HCPs) regarding operative components of the model. Methods: A 26-item questionnaire was prospectively administered to women hospitalized from the 22nd week of gestation (antenatal, early labor, or immediate postpartum) and to obstetric HCPs, primarily obstetricians and nurse-midwives, in three obstetric wards. Four core items addressed key aspects of the IObM model: the source of and indications for referral to IObM treatments, preferred IObM modalities, and willingness to receive care from uncertified IObM providers. Results: The two respondent groups (63 parturient women and 60 HCPs; response rate 95 and 100%, respectively) showed similar patterns regarding language, religiosity, spiritual relatedness, prior complementary medicine use (>66%), and perceived effectiveness and risks during pregnancy and labor. Internal consistency within each of the four core items was moderate and acceptable (parturients, α = 0.61-0.69; HCPs, α = 0.62-0.68). HCPs showed greater support than parturients for nurse-midwife referrals (p = 0.002) and mind-body trained therapies (p = 0.002). Both groups recommended labor-related indications for IObM referral, primarily labor pain, anxiety, and labor progression. Parturients were more supportive of nurse-provided IObM care (p = 0.012). Conclusions: Exploring expectations of parturient women and HCPs is essential when designing IObM models of care. Four core aspects should be prioritized: source of and indication for the referral to IObM treatments and mapping of preferred IObM modalities and providers. These findings reflect acceptability, expectations, and preferences in a single center with an established integrative service and should not be read as evidence of clinical effectiveness or of successful implementation. Further prospective research should explore implementation of these models in real-life practice, assessing effectiveness, risks, and birth experience.

papers.title: Cost-effectiveness of recommended interventions for managing low back pain: A systematic review.
papers.authors: Mathieson S, Underwood M, Ibrahim M, Hua Z, Zhu Z, Ferreira PH et al.
papers.abstract:
Low back pain is the leading cause of disability worldwide. Although numerous treatment approaches are recommended by international clinical guidelines, there is still limited understanding of which interventions provide the best value for money. We aimed to critically appraise and summarise the evidence on the cost-effectiveness and costs of interventions endorsed in recent guidelines to manage low back pain (LBP), compared to usual care.
We searched 10 electronic databases (e.g., MEDLINE (OvidSP), EMBASE (OvidSP), PsycINFO (OvidSP)) from inception to 9th of February 2026 for cost-effectiveness studies of guideline-recommended treatments to manage non-specific LBP. The primary outcome was cost/quality-adjusted life year (QALY), which was converted to 2024 Great British Pound values, tabulated and summarised qualitatively. Secondary outcomes were direct costs (total, interventional, health service use, community services and out-of-pocket costs) and indirect costs (e.g., lost wages, lost productivity, absenteeism). We assessed methodological quality using the Consensus Health Economics Criteria (CHEC) checklist for within-trial economic evaluations or the Philips checklist for modelling studies. Our review included 20 studies (17 within-trial economic evaluations and three modelling studies), published between 2005 and 2026. Half (n = 10) focussed on chronic LBP (>3-month duration), and eight included mixed populations (i.e., acute, subacute and chronic). All studies were of non-pharmacological, non-surgical interventions, both single-modality and multimodal interventions (e.g., exercise plus spinal manipulation; diet plus physical activity). Most interventions are cost-effective at a willingness-to-pay threshold of £20,000. Moreover, interventions aiming to reduce fear and stress or support self-management in people with chronic LBP, as well as clinician-delivered interventions including yoga, acupuncture, cognitive therapy and self-management support are potentially cost-saving from the healthcare, societal and payer's perspectives, as they are both more effective and less costly than usual care (e.g., first contact management, including advice and medication). All of the evidence is derived from high-income countries, and from a considerable heterogenous body of literature. Evidence on cost-effective treatments in low- and middle-income countries remains limited.
Non-pharmacological, non-surgical interventions that include education, psychological support, acupuncture and exercise seem to be cost-effective for managing LBP, compared to usual care. Improved access to and implementation of these effective treatments is urgently needed so more people can benefit from them in routine care.
The review was registered on PROSPERO (https://www.crd.york.ac.uk; CRD42024510270).

papers.title: XuanBi Mitigates Rheumatoid Arthritis via Regulation of ECM-Receptor Interactions and IL-17 Signaling: Insights From Integrated Proteomic and Pharmacological Analyses.
papers.authors: Zhu H, Pan Z, Lu Y, Xia P, He W, Zeng J et al.
papers.abstract: Plant-derived polyphenols possess broad anti-inflammatory activities and may benefit chronic inflammatory diseases. XuanBi is a traditional Chinese medicine formula containing orally absorbable polyphenolic constituents and is used to treat rheumatoid arthritis (RA). This study investigated its absorbable components and potential mechanisms associated with synovial inflammatory hyperplasia. XuanBi was evaluated in collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) rats and rheumatoid arthritis synovial fibroblasts (RASFs). Constituents in the decoction and rat serum were characterized by high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole-Orbitrap mass spectrometry (HPLC-Q-Orbitrap-MS). Predicted targets were intersected with synovial differentially expressed proteins (DEPs), followed by network pharmacology, Gene Ontology (GO), Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses, and experimental validation. Twenty-six absorbable constituents were identified, including catechin, quercetin, baicalein, and wogonin, together with 14 candidate proteins associated with RA synovial pathology. Enrichment analysis implicated extracellular matrix (ECM)-receptor interaction, focal adhesion, and interleukin-17 (IL-17) signaling. Medium- and high-dose XuanBi reduced joint swelling, synovial hyperplasia, and inflammatory infiltration in CIA rats. In RASFs, XuanBi inhibited proliferation, migration, and invasion. It also downregulated fibronectin 1 (FN1) and caveolin 1 (CAV1), reduced phosphorylation of SRC, focal adhesion kinase (FAK), and FYN, decreased integrin alpha 2b (ITGA2B)+/integrin beta 1 (ITGB1)+ cells, and reduced interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β), interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-α), matrix metallopeptidase 3 (MMP3), and matrix metallopeptidase 9 (MMP9). Overall, XuanBi exerted anti-inflammatory and anti-synovial-hyperplasia effects in experimental RA, accompanied by changes in proteins associated with these pathways, supporting the potential involvement of these pathways and warranting further mechanistic and clinical investigation.

papers.authors: Li J, Yang C, Zhang J, Yang L, Hang T, Wang X et al.
papers.abstract:
This randomized controlled trial evaluated the effects of acupuncture on oligomenorrhea in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), and assessed its safety.
International, multicenter, parallel, two-arm randomized controlled trial.
Three outpatient centers in China and the Republic of Korea.
Women aged 20-40 years diagnosed with PCOS (Rotterdam criteria) and oligomenorrhea (cycles >35 days or <8 episodes/year). Of 99 screened, 60 were enrolled and randomized (30/group); two control group participants were subsequently excluded from the full analysis set due to baseline misdiagnosis. Twenty-two (73.3%) in the acupuncture group and 25 (83.3%) in the control group completed the trial.
The acupuncture group received 40 sessions of manual acupuncture over 16 weeks at standardized acupoints, plus usual care (lifestyle advice). The control group received usual care alone.
The primary outcome was the mean change in menstrual frequency (menstruations/month) from baseline to week 16. Secondary outcomes included menstrual cycle length, body mass index (BMI), hormonal profiles, and adverse events, and these were considered exploratory.
In the full analysis set (acupuncture, n=30; control, n=28), acupuncture significantly improved menstrual frequency vs control (mean difference: 0.20; 95% CI: 0.11 to 0.28; p=0.002). Significant improvements favoring acupuncture were also observed for menstrual cycle length (mean difference: -19.69 days; 95% CI: -29.42 to -9.97; p<0.001). No serious adverse events occurred. At week 32, the improvement in menstrual frequency was not sustained (mean difference: 0.14; 95% CI: -0.06 to 0.34; p=0.646).
Acupuncture was associated with short-term improvements in menstrual frequency and cycle length, with no serious adverse events reported, but these improvements were not sustained at week 32. Given the pilot nature of this study, these findings should be considered preliminary.
NCT04509817 (ClinicalTrials.gov).

papers.title: Targeted Modulation of Gut Microbiota: A New Perspective on Acupuncture for the Treatment of Knee Osteoarthritis.
papers.authors: Duan W, Zhang W, Wei N, Liu F, Jiang T, Lai X et al.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota and its metabolites play a key role in the pathological progression of knee osteoarthritis (KOA). Acupuncture may reshape gut‑microbiota profiles, repair intestinal barrier integrity and regulate immune system. Elucidating such biological effects would facilitate a systematic comprehension of the gut‑joint axis as a mediating factor in the pathogenesis and progression of KOA, as well as further mechanistic exploration of acupuncture acting through this gut‑joint axis. In recent years, a growing body of in vivo and in vitro studies has begun to offer insights into the potential mechanisms by which acupuncture may affect KOA through modulation of the gut microbiota. Therefore, it would be valuable to synthesize the existing literature on the possible role of the gut microbiota in acupuncture's effects on KOA. This will deepen our understanding of the biological effects underlying acupuncture‑based interventions. In this review, we emphasize that the regulation of acupuncture on the gut-joint axis involves multiple targets, including the types of intestinal flora, intestinal barrier function, intestinal flora metabolites, immune response, and the role of acupuncture at its own acupoints and clinical program design. Nevertheless, our review of the relevant literature indicates that the current evidence remains primarily at the preclinical stage. And there is still a lack of conclusive clinical evidence to support the hypothesis that modulating the gut microbiota is one of the mechanisms by which acupuncture exerts its therapeutic effects. Accordingly, we discuss future research directions focusing on acupoint compatibility and acupuncture parameters protocol design to decipher potential mechanisms of acupuncture modulating the gut‑joint axis interfere with KOA. This review may provide references for ongoing and future studies of acupuncture for KOA as well as for developing gut-joint-axis-centred acupuncture therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Molecular docking-based screening of natural antifungal compounds targeting a potassium ion channel for modulating Aspergillus carbonarius growth and ochratoxin A production.
papers.authors: Ji Y, Yang S, Zhang Y, Wang X, Li W, Han D et al.
papers.abstract: Fungal contamination and mycotoxin production pose significant threats to global agriculture and human health. Natural products have received widespread attention in controlling fungi and mycotoxin contamination due to their safe and efficient antifungal activities. However, limited knowledge of their molecular targets hinders the rational development of natural antifungal agents. Computational approaches like virtual screening can accelerate discovery by targeting critical fungal proteins. Potassium channels emerge as promising candidates since ion dysregulation triggers fungal apoptosis. Here, we predicted 3D model of Aspergillus carbonarius voltage-gated potassium channel (KvAC) and virtually screened the Traditional Chinese Medicine Systems Pharmacology (TCMSP) database, identifying 13 candidates. Antifungal assays identified two potent compounds: neoglycyrol and evodiamine. Neoglycyrol and evodiamine inhibited A. carbonarius ochratoxin A synthesis by 85% and 51%, respectively. Both compounds also reduced the expression of OTA biosynthetic genes, including pks, nrps, p450, hal, and bZIP, consistent with the reduction in OTA production. To elucidate their mechanism, full-length KvAC (104 kDa) was expressed in CHO-K1 cells. Using PBFI fluorescence probes, both compounds affected intracellular potassium dynamics via KvAC in transfected CHO-K1 cells and A. carbonarius, supporting potassium channel- participated antifungal mechanisms. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that neoglycyrol and evodiamine form stable complexes with KvAC, engaging additional hydrogen bonds and alkyl interactions. Our findings suggest that KvAC may represent a potential molecular target associated with fungal growth and OTA production. It establishes a structure-guided strategy to develop natural antifungal substances, providing a promising strategy for mycotoxin control and safe food preservation.

papers.title: Integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomics with virtual knockout analysis identifies FOS as an epithelial-associated candidate gene in chronic atrophic gastritis.
papers.authors: Li S, Duan H, Liu X, Shan M, Shen Z, Wu M et al.
papers.abstract: Chronic atrophic gastritis (CAG) is a precancerous lesion characterized by epithelial injury, glandular atrophy, and impaired gastric function. Molecular targets linking epithelial alterations with potential traditional Chinese medicine-derived compounds remain unclear. GEO bulk transcriptomic datasets were analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs), which were intersected with CAG-related genes for enrichment analysis. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis and reverse network pharmacology were used to identify key targets and construct a drug-component-target network. Single-cell RNA sequencing, virtual knockout, molecular docking, CCK-8 assay, and RT-qPCR in 1‑Methyl‑3‑nitro‑1‑nitrosoguanidine (MNNG)-treated GES-1 cells were then integrated to prioritize and evaluate FOS. A total of 502 DEGs and 54 intersected CAG-related genes were identified, with enrichment in wound healing, epithelial junction organization, tight junctions, cAMP signaling, gastric cancer, and digestive or secretory pathways. Five key genes-APOA1, CFTR, FOS, HMOX1, and VIM-were identified, all with AUCs above 0.80. Among 21,679 single cells, FOS was the only key gene predominantly enriched in gastric epithelial cells. Virtual knockout predicted associations between FOS-network perturbation and five genes involved in hormone processing and gastric secretory pathways. Docking generated candidate fisetin-FOS and kaempferol-FOS poses for preliminary compound prioritization. MNNG reduced GES-1 cell viability and significantly increased FOS mRNA expression. Integrated computational analyses highlighted FOS as an epithelial-associated candidate gene in CAG and suggested exploratory associations with gastric secretory pathways. These findings support further functional and compound-intervention studies of the FOS/AP-1 axis.

papers.title: Traditional Chinese medicine in CKD: myths, facts, and evidence.
papers.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
papers.authors: Chen Q, Liang Y, Bai J, Chen Z, Zhou J
papers.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) is increasingly used among patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), particularly in regions where healthcare resources, accessibility and cultural acceptance influence treatment choices. However, its role in the treatment of CKD remains controversial, with conflicting perceptions ranging from therapeutic promise to concerns regarding unproven efficacy and potential toxicity. In this review, we critically examine some myths and facts surrounding TCM use in CKD through the framework of evidence-based medicine. Randomized evidence remains limited, but a few trials have reported clinically relevant signals. In patients with type 2 diabetes and CKD, the multicenter SCHEMATIC trial found that add-on Rehmannia-6-based Chinese medicine was associated with a slower decline in eGFR over 48 weeks. In membranous nephropathy, an earlier multicenter randomized trial of Shenqi particle reported reductions in proteinuria and remission outcomes comparable with conventional immunosuppressive therapy. These findings are hypothesis-supporting rather than definitive: neither trial established a reduction in kidney failure, cardiovascular events or mortality, and independent confirmation is lacking. Importantly, safety should not be inferred from natural origin or historical use. Product quality, botanical authentication, pharmacokinetics, toxicological evaluation, herb-drug interactions and pharmacovigilance are essential components of responsible clinical evaluation. Future research should move beyond the broad question of whether 'TCM works' and instead focus on product-specific assessment using rigorous trial methodology, standardized manufacturing, precision CKD phenotyping and internationally applicable outcome measures. Chinese herbal medicines should neither be dismissed solely because they are traditional nor accepted solely because they are natural. Their future role in CKD care should be determined by the same principles applied to any therapeutic intervention: reproducible quality, demonstrated clinical benefit and an acceptable benefit-risk profile.

papers.title: Mechanism of Action of Qingjin Huazhuo Formula in Treating Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Based on Proteomics, Traditional Chinese Medicine Component Analysis, and Network Pharmacology.
papers.authors: Li C, Dong Y, Huang L, Wu W, Wang B, Wang W et al.
papers.abstract: Qingjin Huazhuo Formula (QJHZF) is a traditional Chinese medicinal prescription used to treat chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). To investigate its mechanism of action, a COPD rat model with phlegm heat and blood stasis syndrome was established by combining cigarette smoke exposure and passive swimming. After model confirmation, QJHZF was intragastrically administered at 10.9 g/kg/day for 14 days. The serum inflammatory cytokines and pulmonary oxidative stress indicators in rats were measured using ELISA and biochemical assays, respectively. Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry was performed for proteomic analysis of lung tissues and identification of QJHZF components. Network pharmacology predicted potential targets for COPD treatment. After identifying the core targets through intersection analysis of proteomic targets and network pharmacology targets, qRT-PCR and molecular docking were subsequently employed for validation. Results indicate that QJHZF can inhibit inflammation and reduce oxidative stress associated with COPD. Overall, 114 differentially expressed proteins were identified. In QJHZF, 160 active compounds were identified, with 2,178 possible QJHZF targets involved in COPD treatment. A total of 29 compounds targeting 28 core targets were ultimately identified as the key constituents of QJHZF in treating COPD. qRT-PCR and molecular docking confirmed their pivotal role. KEGG enrichment analysis showed significant enrichment of the core targets in 15 pathways implicated in COPD-related inflammation and oxidative stress. Therefore, this study provides preliminary evidence for a multi-level network of 29 components - 28 targets - 15 pathways through which QJHZF treats COPD, laying a valuable foundation for further in-depth investigation.

papers.title: Integrating network pharmacology, genetically informed multi-omics and granulosa-cell experiments identifies dauricine and oleanolic acid as candidate CASP3-modulating compounds of Zhi-Bai-Di-Huang-Wan in female pubertal timing.
papers.authors: Liao CC, Yang SF, Li JM
papers.abstract: Zhi-Bai-Di-Huang-Wan (ZBDHW) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula clinically used for precocious puberty, but its molecular basis remains unclear. Earlier age at menarche (AAM) reflects advanced female pubertal timing and provides a genetically tractable endpoint relevant to precocious puberty. This study aimed to identify ZBDHW-associated molecular targets relevant to pubertal timing by integrating target prediction, Mendelian randomization-based methylation-expression-protein analyses, Bayesian colocalization, network analysis, and granulosa-cell experiments. ZBDHW ingredients and candidate targets were retrieved from BATMAN-TCM 2.0. Summary data-based Mendelian randomization and Bayesian colocalization integrated methylation, expression, and protein quantitative trait loci with the largest European AAM genome-wide association study. Protein-protein interaction analysis assessed network connectivity. KGN human granulosa cells were treated with dauricine or oleanolic acid, and CASP3 mRNA expression was measured by quantitative reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction. CASP3 was the only ZBDHW-associated target showing convergent evidence across gene expression and protein abundance levels, with supportive methylation evidence at cg06796944. Higher genetically predicted CASP3 expression and protein abundance were associated with later AAM, and CASP3 was a central node in the ZBDHW-related protein-protein interaction network. In KGN cells, dauricine increased CASP3 mRNA at 40 and 80 µM, whereas oleanolic acid increased CASP3 mRNA at 200 µM. These findings support a CASP3-centered methylation-expression-protein target axis as a candidate mechanism linking ZBDHW-associated compounds to female pubertal timing, providing genetically informed multi-omics evidence and preliminary granulosa-cell support relevant to the adjunctive use of ZBDHW in precocious puberty.

papers.title: Acupuncture in the emergency department: A retrospective evaluation of patient-reported outcomes and healthcare utilization.
papers.journal: Acupuncture in medicine : journal of the British Medical Acupuncture Society
papers.authors: Luff A, Burns J, Fendrich M, Conway N, Bottari D, Chang E
papers.abstract:
To examine outcomes following acupuncture as a nonpharmacologic option in emergency departments during real-world implementation.
We conducted a retrospective analysis of a quality improvement program offering acupuncture to adult emergency department patients in 2023 across three intervention sites. Controls were drawn from the same emergency departments in 2022 and from matched nonparticipating emergency departments in 2022-2023. We used propensity score matched difference-in-differences models to estimate the average treatment effect on the treated for admission pain change. Secondary outcomes included emergency department analgesic-related discharge prescriptions and 30-day emergency department return or inpatient admissions. Intervention patients reported on pain, anxiety, stress and nausea before and after treatment and completed a brief post-treatment satisfaction survey.
The matched analytic sample included 358 intervention and 2702 matched control encounters. Acupuncture was associated with greater admission pain reduction (average treatment effect on the treated -1.35; 95% confidence interval -1.84 to -0.85). Among intervention patients, the pre- to post-acupuncture pain change averaged 2.4 points on a 0-10 numerical rating scale. There were no differences in discharge opioid or non-opioid prescriptions and no differences in 30-day emergency department returns or inpatient admissions. Satisfaction was high (with 98% indicating they would receive acupuncture again) and 64% stated they would pay out of pocket. Patients reported significant reductions in anxiety, stress and nausea following acupuncture.
In real-world emergency department implementation, acupuncture was feasible and acceptable, and was associated with clinically meaningful within-patient symptom relief and a statistically significant incremental improvement in admission pain compared with usual care. High satisfaction and improvements in anxiety, stress and nausea indicate potential added patient-centered value beyond pain management.

papers.title: [Drug sensitivity analysis of monotherapy and combination therapy with Chinese and Western drugs in lung cancer organoid models].
papers.journal: Zhonghua zhong liu za zhi [Chinese journal of oncology]
papers.authors: Liu M, Zheng J, Li YX, Han B, Jiang ZM, Liu XZ et al.
papers.abstract: Objective: To construct patient-derived lung cancer organoid models and evaluate the sensitivity of the organoids to antitumor monotherapies, active components of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) and combined regimens of Chinese and Western drugs. Methods: A total of 10 pathologically confirmed lung adenocarcinoma specimens were collected from Tianjin Fifth Central Hospital between June 2024 and June 2025, including six surgical tumor tissue specimens and four pleural effusion samples. These samples were cultured in vitro to establish lung cancer organoid models. Morphological examination, hematoxylin and eosin (HE) staining, and immunohistochemical staining were used to verify the consistence between the organoids and their parental tissues. One organoid model with available genomic profiling data (n=1) was subjected to drug sensitivity testing against commonly used antitumor drugs/regimens, and the results were compared with the clinical response. In successfully established organoid models, antitumor monotherapies (5-fluorouracil [5-FU], cisplatin and osimertinib), active components of Chinese drugs (elemene and ginsenoside Rg3) and combined regimens of Chinese and Western drugs (cisplatin plus ginsenoside Rg3 and 5-FU plus ginsenoside Rg3) were applied. Cell viability was assessed, and the half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) and normalized area under the curve (AUC) values were calculated for each treatment to evaluate drug sensitivity. Results: Among the 10 samples, organoids were successfully cultured from 7 samples, and the organoids closely resembled their parental tissues in morphology and molecular marker expression. In one organoid model with increased epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) gene copy number gain and the EGFR p.E746_A750del mutation, sensitivity testing of commonly used antitumor drugs/regimens, including osimertinib, paclitaxel, cisplatin, the GP regimen (gemcitabine plus cisplatin), and the PP regimen (pemetrexed plus cisplatin), showed that osimertinib exhibited potent antitumor activity (IC50=1.91 μmol/L), markedly superior to the other tested drugs, and the results were consistent with the clinical response. After cryopreservation and rivival, the 7 organoid lines were continued cultured and passaged; 3 were successfully recovered. Drug sensitivity analysis of the 3 successfully established lung cancer organoid models revealed that organoids from different sources responded differently to the same drug. Osimertinib and 5-FU showed higher activity in sample 1 and sample 2, respectively, whereas sample 3 was highly resistant to cisplatin. Active components of Chinese drugs used alone showed no significant inhibitory effect, with normalized AUC values all >0.925. Combination treatment showed stronger inhibition effect in all organoid models, and IC50 values decreased to varying degrees compared with monotherapy. In samples 1 and 3, the IC50 values of cisplatin monotherapy were 152.70 and 475.00 μmol/L, respectively, and decreased to 127.30 and 121.50 μmol/L after combination treatment. Among all models, 5-FU had the lowest monotherapy IC50 among the antitumor drugs (28.08 μmol/L), which was further reduced to 11.26 μmol/L after combination treatment. Conclusion: Patient-derived lung cancer organoid models capture interindividual differences in drug sensitivity and provide a feasible approach for rapid in vitro screening of sensitive regimens and for personalized therapeutic strategies, such as combined therapy with Chinese and Western drugs.

papers.title: Safety Assessment of a Periploca chevalieri Browicz Standardized Extract: Oral Toxicity and Genotoxicity Studies.
papers.authors: Lima K, Malmir M, Rocha J, Pinto R, Figueira ME, Duarte MP et al.
papers.abstract: Periploca chevalieri (Apocynaceae Juss.) is an endemic medicinal plant from Cabo Verde that has long been used in traditional medicine, particularly for the management of diabetes and cough. However, to date, no studies focusing on potential adverse effects compromising its safe use have been performed. The present study aimed to investigate the safety profile of a standardized 70% hydroethanolic extract of Periploca chevalieri aerial parts (PcEE) using complementary in vivo and in vitro toxicological approaches. Repeated oral toxicity of PcEE at doses of 170, 600, and 1000 mg/kg body weight was evaluated in CD-1 mice over 14 days. Clinical signs, body weight, and food intake were monitored, as well as important biochemical parameters (hepatic, renal, and pancreatic biomarkers). Genotoxicity was investigated using the bacterial reverse mutation assay (Ames test) with five different strains of Salmonella Typhimurium in the presence and absence of a metabolizing system. The results obtained showed no significant variations (p < 0.05) in body weight of the animals treated with PcEE at all tested doses. Significant changes (p < 0.05) with negligible relevance were observed in the biochemical parameters of PcEE-treated groups compared to the control group. The Ames test results showed that PcEE did not produce genotoxic effects in any of the tested strains at concentrations up to the maximum tested concentration (5 mg/plate). The results obtained are an important step towards the support and validation of the use of P. chevalieri aerial parts in traditional medicine.

papers.title: Health Information-Seeking Behavior Among Hospitalized Patients with Stroke in China: Associations with Social Support, Quality of Life, and Health Literacy.
papers.authors: Yu G, Lu S, Hu W, Liu LX, Li JF, Cui S et al.
papers.abstract:
This single-center cross-sectional study examined health information-seeking behavior (HISB) among hospitalized patients with stroke, a population with substantial information needs during rehabilitation and discharge planning. Evidence remains limited on the joint associations of social support, quality of life, and multidimensional health literacy with HISB.
To characterize overall and domain-specific HISB and examine its associations with social support, quality of life, and health literacy.
We recruited 231 patients from the acupuncture, neurology, and rehabilitation departments of a tertiary hospital in Shenzhen, China, between October 2025 and March 2026. Participants completed the Chinese 43-item HISB Scale, Social Support Rating Scale (SSRS), WHOQOL-BREF, and a 24-item chronic-disease health-literacy scale. Pearson correlations and two-block hierarchical multiple linear regression were used. The WHOQOL-BREF composite was a study-specific sum of four domain scores, not an official WHOQOL-BREF total score.
Mean HISB was 3.27 (SD 0.20; possible range, 1-5). Attitude (4.08 [SD 0.53]) and information needs (3.89 [SD 0.30]) exceeded source use (2.84 [SD 0.60]). Model 2 explained 22.2% of HISB variance (adjusted R 2=0.183). Social support (B=0.012; beta=0.312; 95% CI, 0.007-0.018; P<0.001) and quality of life (B=0.005; beta=0.197; 95% CI, 0.001-0.009; P=0.015) were positively associated with HISB. Total health literacy was not independently associated with HISB (P=0.155). Some sociodemographic coefficients were sensitive to the standard-error estimator, supporting cautious interpretation.
The findings identify cross-sectional associations rather than causal effects. Social support and quality of life were consistently associated with more active HISB, whereas total health literacy was not independently associated after adjustment. Sociodemographic findings were less stable and require replication. Multicenter longitudinal studies are needed to confirm these associations.

papers.title: Dual-target chemical profiling of anti-influenza multi-components from Isatidis Radix via direct binding to neuraminidase and hemagglutinin.
papers.authors: Chen Y, Yang Z, Yang P, Wu F, Wang Y, Wu T et al.
papers.abstract: Isatidis Radix, the root of Isatis indigotica, is a traditional Chinese medicine used against influenza. However, its chemical profile responsible for direct anti-influenza activity remains poorly characterized. This present study aims to classify the anti-influenza constituents of Isatidis Radix and to investigate their direct interactions with the key viral targets, neuraminidase (NA) and hemagglutinin (HA). To this end, a compound library comprising 91 constituents was assembled (78 isolated and 13 acquired), including nine undescribed compounds. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) was employed to assess binding affinities to NA and HA. Antiviral activity of the compound library was validated in influenza A (H1N1)-infected A549 cells, and molecular docking simulations were performed to explore binding modes. SPR screening revealed that 63.7% and 71.4% of the library showed moderate-to-strong binding to NA and HA, respectively, with alkaloids and lignans as the predominant active classes. Notably, compounds 8, 15, 48, and 87 exhibited nanomolar KD values (0.49-4.22 nM for NA; 0.63-6.26 nM for HA), comparable to oseltamivir and arbidol. Cellular assays demonstrated that 76.9% of tested compounds showed antiviral activity (EC50 < 200 μM), with indole alkaloids and glycosylated lignans being most potent. Integrative SPR and cellular data confirmed a positive correlation between dual-target binding and antiviral efficacy. These findings establish that the anti-influenza activity of Isatidis Radix arises from multi-component, multi-target actions on NA and HA, providing a scientific basis for its clinical use and quality control.

papers.title: [Effects of the nitrogen-fixing and phosphate-solubilizing bacterial strain T4 on the growth and rhizosphere environment of Astragalus membranaceus var. mongholicus].
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.authors: Lu G, Zhang S, Wang Y, Shi Z, Niu J, Liang J
papers.abstract: Plant growth promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) play an important role in promoting plant growth and improving soil environment. This is particularly relevant in the context of the current high-quality development of the traditional Chinese medicine industry, where the application of PGPR in the cultivation of medicinal plants contributes to ensuring the quality and safety of medicinal materials and promoting sustainable and high-quality industrial development. In this study, Astragalus membranaceus var. mongholicus was used as the object to explore the effects of nitrogen-fixing and phosphate-solubilizing bacterial strain T4 soaking on the growth of A. membranaceus var. mongholicus seedlings, rhizosphere soil nutrients and enzyme activities, bacterial community structure and assembly mechanism, in order to reveal its growth-promoting mechanism. Therefore, the seeds of A. membranaceus var. mongholicus were inoculated with the nitrogen-fixing and phosphate-solubilizing bacterial strain T4 via seed soaking prior to sowing. After 60 days of growth, the seedlings and rhizosphere soil samples were collected. Seedling growth indices, soil nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium content, as well as soil enzyme activities were determined. A soil microbial library was constructed using 16S rDNA gene sequencing, followed by taxonomic annotation and diversity analysis to compare the differences in species composition among groups. The microbial community assembly process was elucidated using infer community assembly mechanisms by phylogenetic-bin-based null model analysis (iCAMP). The relationship between soil redundancy analysis (RDA), and a species co-occurrence network was constructed. The metabolic functional potential of the microbial community was predicted using PICRUSt2 (phylogenetic investigation of communities by reconstruction of unobserved states). The results showed that inoculation with the nitrogen-fixing and phosphate-solubilizing bacterial strain T4 promoted the growth of A. membranaceus var. mongholicus and improved the soil quality. Compared with the control, the root length, shoot dry weight and root dry weight increased by 32.08%, 64.56% and 84.36%, respectively, while the soil alkali-hydrolyzable nitrogen content, available phosphorus, and soil urease activity increased by 134.09%, 27.00% and 136.39%, respectively. Furthermore, the strain T4 altered the soil bacterial community structure, driving a shift in community assembly from stochastic processes to deterministic processes, and significantly enriched functional bacterial genera such as Arthrobacter, Acinetobacter and Mesorhizobium (P<0.05). Functional prediction showed that the metabolic functions of the microbial community were significantly enhanced in four aspects (P<0.05): reduction in nitrogen loss, enhancement of detoxification capacity, induction of plant resistance, and augmentation of microbial vitality. In summary, the nitrogen-fixing and phosphate-solubilizing bacterial strain T4 promoted the growth of A. membranaceus var. mongholicus by regulating the rhizosphere microecology and improving soil quality. It lays a theoretical and application foundation for the development of special bacterial fertilizer that can effectively improve soil nutrition level and promote the growth of A. membranaceus var. mongholicus.

papers.title: [Research progress on the multi-target modulation of signaling pathways by acupuncture in the treatment of obesity].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Qu W, Jiang Q, Wei D, Zheng X, Zhu M, Liang Y et al.
papers.abstract: Obesity is a complex metabolic disorder induced by multiple factors, including genetics, environment, and lifestyle. The pathogenesis involves dysregulated glucose and lipid metabolism, insulin and leptin resistance, chronic low-grade inflammation, oxidative stress, and abnormal fat accumulation. These alterations are closely associated with aberrant regulation of key signaling pathways such as adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK), Janus kinase 2/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (JAK2/STAT3), Toll-like receptor 4/nuclear factor κB (TLR4/NF-κB), and silent information regulator 1 (SIRT1) signaling network. As a multi-target intervention method, acupuncture therapy has made significant progress in recent years in improving obesity-related pathological conditions and signaling pathway imbalances. This article reviews the regulatory effects of acupuncture on signaling pathways such as AMPK, JAK2/STAT3, TLR4/NF-κB, and SIRT1 signaling network, explores its molecular mechanism of action in improving obesity, and provides a scientific theoretical basis for the clinical application of acupuncture therapy and the optimization of individual weight-loss strategies.

papers.title: [Analysis of the patterns and characteristics of enhanced efficacy and reduced toxicity of acupuncture-medicine combination therapy].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Yang N, Liu Y, Liu C
papers.abstract: Monotherapy often falls short in treating complex diseases effectively, prompting the emergence of integrated treatment models such as acupuncture-medicine combination therapy, which has gained recognition as a significant strategy to improve clinical efficacy while minimizing adverse effects. This paper systematically examines the necessity of integrating acupuncture with pharmacotherapy. By constructing a theoretical framework centered on supplementation and regulation, it delineates the operational principles of acupuncture-medicine combination therapy. It explores the mechanisms underlying the enhanced efficacy of acupuncture-medicine combination therapy from the perspectives of synergy and complementarity, and analyzes its characteristics in toxicity reduction via counteracting mechanisms. The aim of this paper is to provide a theoretical foundation and future directions for research on acupuncture-medicine combination therapy.

papers.title: [Secondary temperature rise effect at Guanyuan (CV4) after moxibustion in patients with primary dysmenorrhea and its influence on therapeutic effect].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Xu W, Xie D, Li H, Chen R
papers.abstract:
To observe the secondary temperature rise effect at Guanyuan (CV4) induced by moxibustion and its correlation with therapeutic efficacy in patients with primary dysmenorrhea (PD).
A total of 170 PD patients were divided into a non-deqi group (n=61) and a deqi group (n=109) according to the presence or absence of deqi sensation during moxibustion at CV4. After propensity score matching, 59 patients were included in each group. All patients received suspended moxibustion at CV4 for 30 min. Skin temperature at CV4 was measured before and after moxibustion. The presence or absence of secondary temperature rise effect after cessation of moxibustion was observed in both groups. Differences in effective deqi time, deqi intensity, and deqi dimensions were compared between patients with and without secondary temperature rise effect in the deqi group. Subsequently, patients in the deqi group received moxibustion treatment for 2 menstrual cycles, with (7±2) days of treatment per menstrual cycle. The short-form McGill pain questionnaire (SF-MPQ) and COX menstrual symptom scale (CMSS) were used to evaluate the influence of secondary temperature rise effect on therapeutic efficacy.
The incidence of secondary temperature rise effect in the deqi group was 59.32% (35/59), which was significantly higher than 3.39% (2/59) in the non-deqi group (P<0.01). In patients with secondary temperature rise effect in the deqi group, the mean degree of secondary temperature rise was (0.54±0.13) ℃, and the peak of secondary temperature rise appeared at (22.06±1.66) min after cessation of moxibustion. The cooling trend after secondary temperature rise was slower than that immediately after moxibustion (P<0.01). Compared with patients without secondary temperature rise effect, those with secondary temperature rise effect had longer effective deqi time (P<0.01), stronger deqi intensity (P<0.01), and higher incidence rates of general comfort emotional experience and autonomic response dimensions (P<0.01). The degree of secondary temperature rise was positively correlated with effective deqi time and deqi intensity (P<0.001). After treatment and at follow-up, SF-MPQ and CMSS scores in both patients with and without secondary temperature rise effect in the deqi group were lower than those before treatment (P<0.01), and scores in patients with secondary temperature rise effect were lower than those in patients without secondary temperature rise effect (P<0.05, P<0.01). The total effective rate was 95.83% (23/24) in patients with secondary temperature rise effect, which was higher than 75.00% (18/24) in patients without secondary temperature rise effect (P<0.05). The degree of secondary temperature rise was positively correlated with therapeutic efficacy (P<0.001).
Moxibustion at CV4 can induce a secondary temperature rise effect after deqi, which is closely related to effective deqi time, deqi intensity, and deqi dimensions. The secondary temperature rise effect at CV4 can further improve the clinical efficacy in PD patients, and a higher degree of secondary temperature rise is associated with better therapeutic effect.

papers.title: [Study on regulatory effects of warm needling moxibustion on chondrocyte senescence in rats with knee osteoarthritis].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Feng T, Li J, Jia Y, Tao Y, Xu J
papers.abstract:
To investigate the effect of warm needling moxibustion on chondrocyte senescence in rats with knee osteoarthritis (KOA), and to compare its efficacy with that of mild moxibustion.
Forty-eight Wistar rats were randomly assigned to 4 groups (n=12):normal, model, mild moxibustion, and warm needling. KOA was induced by intra-articular injection of monosodium iodoacetate (MIA) into the right knee. Rats in the mild moxibustion and warm needling moxibustion groups received interventions at the acupoints "Futu" (ST32) and "Zusanli" (ST36), 30 min per session, once every other day for 4 weeks. After intervention, Lequesne MG scores, the right knee joint horizontal diameter, and right hind paw pain threshold were assessed. Histopathological changes in the rat knee joints were observed by hematoxylin-eosin (HE) and safranin O staining, and were scored using the Mankin's and OARSI systems. Serum contents of interleukin-6 (IL-6), interleukin-18 (IL-18), and matrix metalloproteinase-13 (MMP-13) were measured by ELISA. Immunohistochemistry was performed to detect the expressions of P16INK4A, P21Waf1/Cip1, IL-6, MMP-13, and type Ⅱ collagen (Collagen-Ⅱ) in knee cartilage. Western blot was performed to detect the relative protein expression levels of P16INK4A, P21Waf1/Cip1, Collagen-Ⅱ, IL-6, and MMP-13 in cartilage tissue.
Compared with the normal group, the model group showed a significantly higher Lequesne MG score (P<0.01), an increased horizontal diameter of the right knee joint (P<0.01), and a decreased pain threshold (P<0.01). Compared with the model group, both treatment groups exhibited significantly lower Lequesne MG scores (P<0.01), reduced joint horizontal diameters (P<0.01), and increased pain thresholds (P<0.01). Compared with the mild moxibustion group, the warm needling group showed a lower Lequesne MG score (P<0.01) and a higher pain threshold (P<0.01). Histopathological staining revealed degenerative features in the model group, including damage to the superficial cartilage layer and disappearance of the tidemark, while both treatment groups exhibited milder degeneration. Compared with the normal group, both the Mankin's and OARSI scores were significantly increased in the model group (P<0.01). Compared with the model group, both scores were decreased in the mild moxibustion and warm needling groups (P<0.01), and the scores in the warm needling group were significantly lower than those in the mild moxibustion group (P<0.05). Compared with the normal group, the serum contents of IL-6, IL-18, and MMP-13 were significantly elevated in the model group (P<0.01);in cartilage tissue, the expressions of P16INK4A, P21Waf1/Cip1, IL-6, and MMP-13 proteins were increased (P<0.01), while Collagen-Ⅱ expression was reduced (P<0.01). Compared with the model group, both treatment groups showed decreased serum IL-6, IL-18, and MMP-13 contents, and reduced expression of P16INK4A, P21Waf1/Cip1, IL-6, and MMP-13 proteins in cartilage tissue (P<0.01, P<0.05), along with increased Collagen-Ⅱ expression (P<0.01). Furthermore, compared with the mild moxibustion group, the warm needling group exhibited more significant changes in the above indicators except joint horizontal diameter (P<0.01, P<0.05).
Warm needling moxibustion effectively improves knee osteoarthritis in rats and shows superior efficacy compared with mild moxibustion. Its therapeutic mechanism may be associated with the inhibition of chondrocyte senescence.

papers.title: [Effect of electroacupuncture on the SIRT1/HIF-1α/Nrf2 signaling pathway of thoracic aorta in ApoE-/- atherosclerotic mice].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Luo Y, Hu X, Zeng Y, Zhang N
papers.abstract:
To observe the effect of electroacupuncture(EA) on lipid metabolism, oxidative stress status, pathological morphology of the thoracic aorta and the expression of silent information regulator 1(SIRT1)/hypoxia-inducible factor 1α(HIF-1α)/nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2(Nrf2)signaling pathway in ApoE-/- atherosclerotic(AS)mice, in order to explore the potential mechanism of EA in the prevention and treatment of AS.
Ten C57BL/6J mice were assigned as the control group and fed with normal diet, while 42 SPF-grade male ApoE-/- mice were fed with high-fat diet for 12 weeks to establish an AS model. Following successful model induction, the ApoE-/- mice were randomly divided into model, EA, EA+inhibitor, and agonist groups, with 10 mice per group. The EA group received EA at the acupoints "Neiguan"(PC6), "Tongli"(HT5), and "Zusanli"(ST36) using a sparse-dense wave(2 Hz/15 Hz), with a current intensity of 0.3 mA. Each session lasted for 20 min. The EA+inhibitor group received intraperitoneal injections of the SIRT1 inhibitor EX-527(10 mg/kg), with other treatment identical to that in the EA group. The agonist group received intragastric administration of the SIRT1 agonist resveratrol(50 mg/kg). All interventions were administered every other day for 8 weeks. Body weight was measured once every 4 weeks. Serum levels of triglycerides(TG), total cholesterol(TC), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol(HDL-C), and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol(LDL-C), as well as the oxidative stress markers superoxide dismutase(SOD), malondialdehyde(MDA), and glutathione peroxidase(GSH-Px)were measured using colorimetric assays. Histopathological changes in the aorta were assessed using hematoxylin-eosin(HE)staining. The protein and mRNA expression levels of SIRT1, HIF-1α, and Nrf2 in the aorta were analyzed by Western blot and real-time fluorescence quantitative PCR, respectively.
After treatments, compared with the control group, the model group exhibited significantly decreased serum HDL-C, SOD and GSH-Px levels(P<0.01), increased body weight, and serum LDL-C, TC, TG and MDA levels(P<0.01). HE staining showed pathological changes in the vessel wall, including thickened intima with an uneven surface, proliferated endothelial cells forming plaques, inflammatory cell infiltration on the plaque surface, elastic layer structure damage, disordered arrangement of the media smooth muscle layer, and localized foam cells and smooth muscle cell proliferation. Additionally, the protein and mRNA expression levels of SIRT1 and Nrf2 were significantly down-regulated(P<0.01), while those of HIF-1α were up-regulated(P<0.01). Compared with the model group, both the EA and agonist groups showed increased serum HDL-C, SOD and GSH-Px levels(P<0.01, P<0.05), decreased body weight, and serum LDL-C, TC, TG and MDA levels(P<0.01). HE staining revealed improved endothelial morphology, with intact vascular wall, relatively smooth intima, a small amount of endothelial cells abscission, regular arrangement of the smooth muscle layer of the media, no obvious damage in the elastic layer structure, and a small amount of foam cells and smooth muscle cells proliferated.The protein and mRNA expression levels of SIRT1 and Nrf2 were significantly increased(P<0.01, P<0.05), while HIF-1α protein and mRNA expression levels were decreased(P<0.01). Compared with the EA group, the EA+inhibitor group showed decreased serum HDL-C, SOD and GSH-Px levels(P<0.05), increased body weight, and serum LDL-C, TC, TG and MDA levels(P<0.05, P<0.01). HE staining showed that the structural integrity of the vascular wall was damaged, with thickening and injury of the endometrium, endothelial cell proliferation plaques and infiltration of inflammatory cells on the plaque surface, disordered arrangement of smooth muscle layer, and obvious proliferation of smooth muscle cells. The protein and mRNA expression levels of SIRT1 and Nrf2 were significantly reduced(P<0.01, P<0.05), while those of HIF-1α were increased(P<0.01, P<0.05).
EA may regulate lipid metabolism, alleviate oxidative stress injury, promote vascular intimal repair, and delay the progression of AS in ApoE-/- mice through the activation of the SIRT1/HIF-1α/Nrf2 antioxidant signaling pathway.

papers.title: [Research progress on the autonomic-immune mechanism of acupuncture in regulating ovarian function].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Huang Y, Xu T, Li C, Yuan Y, Xia Y
papers.abstract: Ovarian dysfunction is an important cause of ovulatory disorders, infertility and endocrine disorders in women, which is commonly observed in conditions including polycystic ovary syndrome, primary ovarian insufficiency, diminished ovarian reserve and ovarian aging-related states. Recent studies have demonstrated that besides abnormalities in the classic hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis, autonomic nervous imbalance and immune-inflammatory disturbance also serve as critical mechanisms underlying impaired ovarian function. Central inflammatory responses, chronic stress and metabolic abnormalities can disrupt hypothalamic rhythmic regulation, augment sympathetic nerve output and induce local chronic low-grade ovarian inflammation, consequently contributing to follicular developmental disorders and aberrant steroidogenesis. As a neuromodulation therapy initiated by somatic sensory input, acupuncture can modulate central integration via the "spinal cord-brainstem-hypothalamus" pathway, thereby regulating autonomic nervous activity and immune-inflammatory responses and improving the local ovarian microenvironment. Existing evidence suggests that acupuncture may exert its effects by inhibiting sympathetic overactivation, recruiting vagus-related anti-inflammatory pathways, modulating immune cell polarization, and alleviating oxidative stress and apoptosis. This paper reviews research progress from three aspects: the autonomic-immune regulatory basis of ovarian function, pathological imbalance characteristics, and intervention mechanisms of acupuncture, so as to provide references for neuroimmune-targeted intervention of ovarian dysfunction and acupuncture mechanism research.

papers.title: [Explanation on modern mechanism of "for abdominal-diseases, Zusanli is indicated": acupuncture at Zusanli (ST36) regulates the brain-gut "neuro-immune axis" for the treatment of diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome].
papers.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
papers.authors: Ma J, Chen Y, Xia Y
papers.abstract: Diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) is a functional intestinal disorder characterized by recurrent abdominal pain, diarrhea and altered defecation habits. It is frequently comorbid with psychological disorders such as anxiety and depression, which greatly impair the quality of life. Accumulating evidence demonstrates that the core pathological links of IBS-D involve disrupted brain-gut interaction and dysregulation of the brain-gut "neuro-immune axis", including visceral hypersensitivity, low-grade mucosal inflammation, impaired intestinal barrier function, gut microbiota dysbiosis and abnormal autonomic nerve modulation. Zusanli (ST36) is an essential acupoint for digestive disorders, and the ancient maxim "for abdominal-diseases, Zusanli is indicated" summarizes its prominent clinical value in abdominal ailments. Modern studies have verified that acupuncture at ST36 can remodel vagal-sympathetic balance via the peripheral afferent-central integration-autonomic efferent circuit, modulate central nociceptive and emotional processing, and exert regulatory effects on brain-gut peptide signals such as 5-hydroxytryptamine, suppress immune activation and release of inflammatory mediators, improve the expression of tight-junction proteins and intestinal mucosal permeability, as well as modulate microbiota-metabolite-related pathways. Thereby, it attenuates the neuro-immune feedback of "stress-inflammation-pain amplification", alleviates visceral hypersensitivity and relieves symptoms including abdominal pain and diarrhea. Taking the classical maxim "for abdominal-diseases, Zusanli is indicated" as a clue, this paper reviews research advances regarding acupuncture at ST36 in treating IBS-D by regulating the brain-gut "neuro-immune axis". Limitations of current evidence are also pointed out, including insufficient circuit verification, unclear stimulus parameter-effect relationship and non-standardized clinical protocols, so as to provide references for standardized application and mechanistic exploration of acupuncture at ST36 in treating functional gastrointestinal disorders.
